decision: '->' then the invoked function, then exactly one of three argument forms: a body, a function reference, or an ordinary argument list. None of the three is optional, so an operation always takes one. The member after '->' is InstantiatedTypeMember; the clause's own InvocationTypeMember is defined nowhere and is a specification defect the editor has acknowledged. See the deviation InvocationTypeMember-misnomer.

evidence.note: why the member after '->' is InstantiatedTypeMember

notes: Was status 'conflict'. Adjudicated on OMG issue KERML11-83, which quotes this rule and reports the technical editor's own account that InvocationTypeMember should have been InstantiatedTypeMember, plus the Pilot's independent use of InstantiatedTypeMember in the corresponding slot and 16 corpus instances of the '->' syntax.
